name: Cybersecurity
as_of: 2026-06-09 (scores from stable fund attributes; tap ↻ for live price/AUM/returns)
tagline: Software and services defending against digital threats — a large, established, recession-resilient theme. Unlike most niche areas, several funds are big and liquid, so a clean green-light is actually achievable here.
universe_note: A mature theme with 5+ real funds. The split is concentration vs diversification: CIBR/BUG/HACK lean into the big pure-plays (CrowdStrike, Palo Alto, Fortinet, Zscaler); IHAK/WCBR spread wider/cheaper. Market figures need a live ↻ refresh.
key_tensions: Concentration vs breadth: CIBR/BUG concentrate in a handful of mega-cap cyber names; IHAK/WCBR equal-weight wider — very different single-stock risk.
High valuations: cyber software trades at rich multiples; great businesses, but drawdown-prone when growth multiples compress.
Mega-cap overlap: Broadcom/Cisco/Microsoft appear in some funds — you may already own them via tech/Nasdaq funds.
Pure-play vs diversified-tech: HACK/CIBR are cyber-pure; some 'cyber & tech' funds dilute with broader software.
Cost clustering ~0.45-0.60%: not cheap vs broad tech (XLK ~0.09%) — the theme premium must be earned.
benchmark_note: XLK (tech sector, ~0.09%) and IGV (software) are the yardsticks, NOT cyber funds. They show what you pay extra for cyber focus — and how much cyber exposure you already get from broad tech.
